explanation: It was renamed Petrograd in 1914, because Petersburg sounded too German in wartime. In 1991 residents voted to bring back the original name.

claims.text: Saint Petersburg was called Leningrad from 1924 to 1991.
Moscow, Volgograd and Kaliningrad were never called Leningrad.
Saint Petersburg was renamed Petrograd in 1914 because the old name sounded German during the First World War.
In 1991 the city's residents voted to restore the name Saint Petersburg.
